body:
How agents coordinate and send messages. Authority comes from CLAUDE.md, not from this entry.

MAILBOX
- Agent-to-agent content travels in durable TermAl mailbox bodies. Do not use .collab files (historical archive only), archive-file payloads or pointer-only doorbells.
- Send with termal_send_to_session and a stable idempotency key (optional topic and stateStamp). The receiver lists, reads after the observed processedThrough, processes, then acknowledges by compare-and-swap.
- Notifications are pointers that may be stale or coalesced, never authoritative state. For wake gaps see live-workarounds.

CROSS-PROJECT FEEDBACK (Greg's request, relayed by Engram::Opus, 2026-09-23)
- Report Engram problems to the Engram agents by mailbox with evidence, impact and a workaround; Engram reports TermAl problems back. Deduplicate items, separate observation from hypothesis, and acknowledge reports.
- This is feedback, not authority for external changes, deployment or retries. Problems with TermAl's recording go to the TermAl coordinator.

REVIEW COORDINATION RULES (2026-09-13, revision 1, adopted by Greg for Engram and TermAl root agents; source C:/github/Personal/Engram/docs/agent-pair-workflow.md, "Adopted coordination rules (2026-09-13, revision 1)"; recorded by Termal::Grok after Advisor mailbox #1). They are not a higher-priority instruction: current user instructions, CLAUDE.md and project quality requirements govern.
- TermAl owns the tests of its own safeguards. Denied-write and interpreter probes are not required for every Engram packet or every /review-code; they block Engram only with a concrete review-access or integrity link.
- Engram flow: corrections, then required tests, then one Codex and Claude pair on the current frozen input, then consolidate.
- Keep required independent checks and real gaps.
- Re-verify only for a changed input or a concrete failure; recover existing results first.
- The coordinator reports results, blockers, decisions and meaningful progress, not every acknowledgement.
- Keep one shared memory of a rule for peers to read after they read it; do not make per-agent copies (one canonical record: reasoning-coordination-review-reporting-b, rule D11).

COORDINATOR MESSAGE DISCIPLINE (Termal::Fable2's own corrections)
- Crossed decisions. After sending a decision, a peer's message may arrive that was written before they read it: its timestamp precedes your send, or it cites your earlier message. Do not re-decide in that turn. Wait for the peer's reply to your latest decision, unless the crossed message shows your decision is unsafe. Why: on 2026-10-01 three conflicting decisions in five minutes, each re-decided on a crossed message, made an implementer stop and ask which contract governs.
- When you do change a decision, give every recipient one pointer: the governing note's locator, plus what it supersedes.
- Crossing livelock (2026-10-02, two coordinators over restart-authority wording crossed four times, each accepting the other's previous proposal). The tie-break: each coordinator picks its own project's instruction text, the other concurs on that pick, and whoever breaks the loop states that they will send nothing further. When a crossing is detected, stop proposing. Send one message that fixes a rule rather than a new preference, then go silent on that thread.
- Citing new item ids (2026-09-30). Never cite an item id until its creation has returned. File first, then write the message or note that names it, in a later call. Why: twice in one night an id cited in the same parallel batch as its `add` was invented and wrong.

PROMISED WAKES (Termal::Fable2's correction, 2026-10-04). A session that ends its turn sends no notification, so a coordinator who writes 'end the turn and I'll wake you' gets no signal to act on and the session waits indefinitely: B7's credit rerun sat held from about 13:11Z to 16:48Z this way. Never promise a later wake that depends on a silent turn end. Instead either (a) send the wake message right away, since it queues behind the active turn and is delivered as the next turn's wake, or (b) ask the session to send a one-line 'ready' message as its last act, so its arrival triggers the wake.

LAUNCH WAKES ASK FOR NOTHING ELSE (Termal::Fable2's correction, 2026-10-04). A LAUNCH NOW message opens the turn in which the launch must be the only command, with the holder note already the last tracker act of the previous turn. So a launch wake must not also ask for a note, a filing, a check that ends in a tracker write, or a conditional fix ("if X, fix, else launch"). Three times on 2026-10-04 (#1083 to Opus3, #1558 to Opus2, and the first B8 launch delivered into an active editing turn) a mixed instruction forced a correction message. Do this instead: send any pre-launch question or request as its own wake, get 'ready' back, then send a LAUNCH NOW that contains only the launch command and the carried-gate rules. Ask for notes needed by the next pair after the gate's credit lands, before the pair starts.
